counter_arguments: The PR modifies webhook duplicate handling, not the charge amount logic where the cap is applied.
The workaround HACK-008 is tied to a downstream ledger overflow; the PR does not change any ledger schema, data types, or amount processing.
Revisit condition for HACK-008 is the completion of ticket PAY-240 (ledger migration to bigint). The PR closes ticket PAY-212, unrelated to the ledger migration.
No code changes touch the `if amount > 50000:` block or any related financial calculation; the diff only adds SQLite idempotency code.
Even if the PR indirectly affects downstream processing, it does not address the root cause (int column overflow) that the cap was protecting against.
reasoning: The PR under review introduces database-backed idempotency for Stripe webhook events, replacing an in-memory set. The workaround HACK-008 concerns capping charge amounts to avoid integer overflow in a ledger table, with the condition to remove the cap only after a bigint migration (PAY-240). Since the PR does not modify the amount-capping logic, the ledger schema, or any related financial processing, it does not satisfy the revisit condition and therefore does not resolve the workaround.
